raw_response:
I'm 73 this year. I've been working these fields since I was 23 — fifty years. It's just me and my wife now, two mouths to feed on five mu of land. Our son is in Shijiazhuang doing construction, sends a little money now and then, but I don't count on that for farming. I count on what I know, and what I've seen with my own eyes.

I split my five mu three and two. Three mu I do wheat then maize, same as always. The other two mu I still plant cotton, though honestly at my age the picking is getting hard. My back isn't what it used to be. But my wife says we might as well keep the cotton — the wheat and maize money is for grain, the cotton money is for cash expenses.

**Wheat** — I plant around October 8th, right after Cold Dew. I use the improved seed I bought last autumn, kept it dry in the shed. I plow the three mu once with the small tractor, then broadcast the seed. Before planting I put down one bag of compound fertilizer per mu — about 50 jin — and work it into the soil. That's my base. Then in March, when the wheat turns green, I walk the fields. If it looks a bit yellow, I topdress with half a bag of urea, about 25 jin per mu. Some years I skip the topdress if the wheat looks vigorous, but last year I skipped it and regretted it. This year I'll do it. I irrigate three times: green-up, jointing, and grain filling. The pump electricity isn't cheap, but my neighbor Wang only did two times last spring and his yield was down. I harvest around June 10th. I expect about 400 jin per mu — not spectacular, but steady.

**Maize** — Right after wheat harvest, mid-June, sometimes within two or three days. I don't have time to plow deep. If the weather allows I run the rotary tiller once, but some years I plant directly into the wheat stubble. I buy hybrid seed every year, about 5 jin per mu. I put fertilizer down at planting — compound fertilizer and a bit of urea, all at once. Summer maize grows fast, and honestly I don't have the energy to chase after it like I do with wheat. I irrigate twice if it doesn't rain: once when it's knee-high, and once at tasseling. The summer rains usually help. Harvest before National Day, around September 28th. I hope for 450 jin per mu.

**Cotton** — I plant in late April, around the 25th. I till those two mu properly, cotton likes loose soil. I put down less fertilizer than wheat — about 40 jin of compound per mu, one time at planting. Cotton needs more spraying though. The bollworm comes every year without fail. I spray insecticide three, maybe four times, and herbicide once. I irrigate twice: before flowering and when the bolls are forming. Picking starts in September and goes through October, three or four rounds. My wife and I do it all by hand. It's slow. We get about 250 jin per mu of seed cotton. I thought about giving up cotton, but the price last year was decent, so I keep it.

I don't hire labor. Cannot afford it. Family labor only. My wife handles some of the fertilizer spreading and cotton picking. I do the plowing, planting, and heavy work. Our total spending on seeds, fertilizer, electricity for water, and pesticide will be about 1,650 yuan this year. That's a lot for us, but I have a little cash put aside from last autumn's maize sale. I won't spend more than that — at my age I need to keep some money for medicine and emergencies. Better safe than sorry.
